2027 Kawasaki Ninja 650 ABS Sportbike Adds Upgraded Suspension and Brakes
14 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
This week marked the start of an invasion of motorcycles made by Japanese Kawasaki. In a single move, the bike maker announced that some 33 two-wheelers are returning for the new model year with minor changes compared to their previous incarnations and slight price adjustments. At the same time, though, four others are coming back with many new things in the bag.
One of the machines that got a significant revamp this week is the Ninja 650 ABS middleweight sportbike. While still retaining the same trellis frame and 649cc parallel-twin engine working a six-speed transmission as before, it now throws in an upgraded suspension system, tweaked brakes, a new instrument display layout, and, for the first time, a very handy option.
The suspension setup changes are, perhaps, the most extensive. Kawasaki opted to go for a new Showa 37mm SFF-BP inverted fork at the front, with settings specifically tailored to maintain the same riding feel as before.
The hardware at the back is the same as it used to be, only this time it comes with revised spring and damping settings for the horizontal back-link setup, a reduced spring rate, and optimized initial preload. These changes should enhance, first and foremost, cornering stability.
When it comes to the braking system, Japanese engineers opted to install radial-mount four-piston front brake calipers instead of the previous axial-mount two-piston units. On top of that, the ABS calibration has changed.
There is now expanded smartphone connectivity to go with the motorcycle, bringing updated navigation and voice commands, including searching destinations, adding waypoints, and changing route order.
Then, an updated 4.3-inch TFT color instrument panel with two display layouts shows info on things like speed, engine rpm, gear position, and pretty much everything that has to do with the two-wheeler.
There is a visual change as well that is introduced by the refreshed Ninja 650, and that comes as a wider front fender that covers more of the fork outer tubes. Then, the seat position now stands 30.9 inches (780 mm) off the ground, allowing for a relatively upright riding position.
When it comes to the accessories available for the motorcycle, Kawasaki is throwing in, for the first time, the Kawasaki Quick Shifter (KQS) that allows the bike to upshift without the use of the clutch, as long as the engine operates above 2,500 rpm.
Kawasaki says the 2027 Ninja 650 ABS lands on American dealer lots by the end of October, and that it will sell in four color combinations: Lime Green, Galaxy Silver, Metallic Matte Twilight Blue/Candy Persimmon Red, and Metallic Flat Spark Black/Metallic Carbon Gray.
Depending on the color chosen, the motorcycle will set people back $8,099 for standard hues, or $8,299 for the special colors and graphics.
